page: Amazon Web Services r5b.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is driven by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, providing 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache. The system provides 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. There is no integrated local storage or discrete GPU hardware included, while network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional memory subsystem capability, with uncached 256 MB read bandwidth reaching 223.47 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieving 98.11 GB/sec, placing large-block memory transfers in the upper performance tier. Multi-core compute performance tests consistently within middle percentiles, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11786.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 41628.77. Single-threaded execution presents a performance tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core throughput and compression benchmarks ranking in lower tiers. In-memory transaction benchmarks remain steady, evidenced by 50.94 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The qualitative efficiency of the r5b.16xlarge resides in its high memory density rather than raw per-core CPU performance. Organizations running workloads bound by RAM capacity benefit from the 512 GB footprint, whereas workloads requiring high single-thread clock speeds or local disk IOPS will experience bottlenecks. This server configuration is suited for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caching layers, ETL pipelines, and in-memory analytics systems.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and 512 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz. The hardware contains no local storage volumes and no discrete GPUs, utilizing a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-tier uncached memory bandwidth alongside standard mid-range multi-core CPU capacity. Single-core processing and text generation tasks demonstrate lower throughput, representing a clear performance tradeoff. With an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation, this configuration aligns with memory-heavy enterprise deployments, including large in-memory key-value stores, relational database management systems, and data processing platforms that do not depend on integrated local disk storage.
